about: The coding agents and apps bmoe-server can serve (GET /api/connect, docs/agent.md). Placeholders: {{origin}} is the server's address, {{base_url}} its OpenAI-compatible base ({{origin}}/v1), {{model}} the loaded model's id, {{api_key}} 'local' when the server has no key and a pointer to it when it has one. `write` says how POST /api/connect/<id> writes `file`: toml_block replaces a marked block of its own, json_merge merges the snippet's object into the file's. `acp`, on a coding agent, is how the desktop runs it as a conversation's agent over the Agent Client Protocol (GET /api/agent): the command and its arguments, and the programs that must be on PATH for it to be offered. An entry with no snippet is not listed under Connect.

clients.name: Claude Code
clients.how: Claude Code speaks the Anthropic Messages API, which this server serves. Set these in the shell you start it from. Load the model with a context of at least 32768 tokens.

clients.name: Codex CLI
clients.how: Codex CLI speaks the OpenAI Responses API. This adds a `bmoe` provider and profile to its config: start it with `codex --profile bmoe`, with BMOE_API_KEY set to {{api_key}}.
clients.snippet:
[model_providers.bmoe]
name = "BigMoeOnEdge"
base_url = "{{base_url}}"
wire_api = "responses"
env_key = "BMOE_API_KEY"

[profiles.bmoe]
model = "{{model}}"
model_provider = "bmoe"

clients.name: OpenCode
clients.how: Adds this server as an OpenAI-compatible provider in OpenCode's global config. The key is read from BMOE_API_KEY ({{api_key}}); pick the model as bmoe/{{model}}.

clients.name: Pi
clients.how: Pi, a minimal coding agent, through its ACP adapter. Install Pi itself and Node.js; point Pi at this server as an OpenAI-compatible provider ({{base_url}}, key {{api_key}}) in Pi's own settings.

clients.name: OpenAI SDK (Python)
clients.how: Any program that uses an OpenAI client library works with the base URL and key below.
clients.snippet:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="{{base_url}}", api_key="{{api_key}}")
reply = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="{{model}}",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
)
print(reply.choices[0].message.content)

clients.name: Open WebUI
clients.how: In Open WebUI, open Admin Settings, Connections, and add an OpenAI API connection with these values. From a container, use the host's address instead of 127.0.0.1 (start this server with --host and --api-key-file for that).
